newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's Samir refinery's profit to rise 10.6 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's Samir refinery's profit to rise 10.6 pct in 1996.

text.p: Net profit of Morocco's Samir oil refinery is expected to rise by 10.6 percent in 1996 to 468 million dirhams ($50.8 million), Upline Securities stockbroker said on Tuesday.
Samir is to post a 7.4 billion dirhams ($808 million) turnover in 1996, up 10.8 percent over the previous year, Upline said in a report. The firm's turnover was 6.6 billion dirhams in 1995.
"For the whole fiscal year of 1996, Samir is expected to post a net income of 468 million dirhams," Upline said.
The firm's net income was 423 million dirhams in 1995, it said.
Samir's 1996 official results are expected to be published in April 1997, an official at the energy ministry said.

Upline said refinery sales volume dropped 5.0 percent in 1996 compared with the previous year, due mainly to the use of coal instead of fuel in Jorf Lasfar power generation plant, located on the Atlantic coast.
Samir refinery, Morocco's biggest, holds 80 percent of the Moroccan market refined petroleum products while Societe Cherifienne des Petroles holds the remaining 20 percent.
SCP has a refinery located in the northern town of Sidi Kacem. The two refineries are among the 113 state-owned companies to be privatised by end 1998.
Societe Marocaine de l'Industrie du Raffinage (Samir) has a processing capacity of 6.25 million tonnes per year.
"Samir plans to expand its production capacity to 8.25 million tonnes per year in future," the report said.
In March 1996, Samir floated 30 percent of its stock on the Casablanca bourse at 243 dirhams per share. After a period of fluctuation, the shares remained stable at the same level.

Negotiations to build a hard core of investors for Samir are still under way since the second half of 1996, a market analyst said. "By June 1997, Samir's hard core of investors will undoubtly be set up," the analyst said.
The government hopes to sell up to 51 percent of Samir's stock to a group of foreign investors to develop and upgrade the firm in future, an official said.
One of the 47 listed stocks on the Casablanca bourse, Samir has a market capitalisation of 4.9 billion dirhams and an average daily trading of 2.73 million dirhams, traders said.
Established in 1959 in the port town of Mohammedia, near Casablanca, Samir has a capital of 813 million dirhams and employs a staff of more than 1,200.
